newsitem.title: UK: Sakura expands investor base with Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: Sakura expands investor base with Eurobond.

text.p: The third largest bank in the world in terms of assets, Sakura Bank Ltd, launched the largest perpetual issue on Thursday via sole lead manager Merrill Lynch.

Syndicate official at Merrill Lynch said Sakura wanted to expand its investor base with the launch of an extensively pre-marketed Eurobond which has a 144a clause, enabling the bonds to be sold immediately to U.S. buyers.

"They wish to diversify their investor base and their source of capital and Merrill came to the borrower and recommended a strong approach towards raising money internationally," the syndicate official said.
"Top priority was given to sales away from Japan," he said, adding Merrill Lynch had been working on the institutionally- targeted deal for at least one month.
"I believe its the largest perpetual debt offering ever for the market and the largest subordinated debt offering that Merrill Lynch has ever underwritten."
The offering was split into two tranches, a fixed-rate tranche for $400 million pays a 7.32 percent coupon. There is a call from February 2002.
Sales distribution saw 80 percent into the U.S. and 20 percent into Europe, Merrill Lynch said.
The floating-rate note tranche for $600 million pays a coupon of three-month LIBOR plus 95 b.p. to February 2002 and then steps up to 245 b.p. if not called from February 2002.
Sales distribution saw 60 percent sell into Europe, 15 percent into the U.S. and 25 percent into non-Japan Asia.
"We still carry a small residual position in both tranches which gives us the opportunity to reach other accounts," the syndicate official said.
The issue is expected to be rated Baa2 by Moody's Investors Service and BBB by Standard & Poor's Corp, while the borrower has a rating of A3/A- by Moody's and S&P.
